name: text-field
summary: A labelled field for a line of text, such as an email address, a password or a search.

properties.name: label
properties.description: What the field is for, shown above it and its spoken name. A placeholder is never the name.

properties.name: placeholder
properties.description: An example of what to type, shown while the field is empty.

properties.name: description
properties.description: Supporting words under the label, read after the name.

properties.name: error
properties.description: What is wrong. The field is invalid while it has one, and its edge turns destructive.

properties.name: type
properties.description: What kind of text it holds; each sets the keyboard and autofill. password adds a show button.

properties.name: variant
properties.description: outline draws the box; plain draws none, for a field in a frame the app draws.

properties.name: size
properties.description: md is 44 points tall; lg is 56 with larger text, for a page's main search.

properties.name: required
properties.description: The field must be filled; the label gets a marker and the name says required.

properties.name: hideLabel
properties.description: Hides the label's words; the field keeps it as its name.

properties.name: clearable
properties.description: Adds a Clear button while there is text.

properties.name: disabled
properties.description: The field and its buttons can't be used.

events.name: submit
events.description: Return or Enter in the field.

states.name: rest
states.description: The edge at 3:1 on the page, so the box can be found.

states.name: focused
states.description: The ring colour, twice as thick.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Faded; its buttons can't be pressed.

accessibility.name: Its label, with required when it is; then its error, then its description.
accessibility.keyboard: One tab stop for the input; Clear and Show password are their own.
accessibility.web: An <input> with a <label>, aria-describedby for the description and error, aria-invalid with an error.
accessibility.apple: SwiftUI's TextField or SecureField, named by its label (", required"), with its error and description as its hint; the words drawn around it are hidden so nothing is read twice.
accessibility.windows: UI Automation ControlType.Edit with the Value pattern, named by its label, help text its error then its description.

cases.person: An Email label with a required marker, a line under it and an empty box.
A Password box showing dots, with an eye button at its end.
A box with a red edge and the error under it.

deviations: Also date and time types, which open the OS picker; native kits use the platform's date picker instead.
startAdornment and endAdornment slots; native kits draw search's magnifying glass and no other adornment yet.
No date or time type: SwiftUI's DatePicker is the control for those.
